$comment: Native 9:16 micro-lesson: Keating teaches the seasons Socratically. Two voices; the learner reaches the answer. Canonical narration; edit a line and re-run produce.sh.
label: KEATING // ONE-MINUTE LESSON
format: micro-lesson — vertical, two-voice Socratic dialogue over animated illustrations

tts.instructions: Voice: a warm, wry teacher mid-lesson with one student, genuinely curious about how they think. Pacing: conversational, a real pause after every question. Pronounce 'Keating' as KEE-ting.

scenes.text: Quick one. Why is it colder in winter?

scenes.instructions: A bright student answering quickly and confidently, a common guess. Natural and casual.
scenes.text: Because the Earth is farther from the sun?
Good guess. Then why is it summer in Sydney when it's winter in Toronto?

scenes.instructions: The same student slowing down, thinking it through out loud, a little surprised at themself.
scenes.text: Oh. Same distance, both places. So it's not distance. Is it the tilt?
Keep going. What does the tilt do to the sunlight?

scenes.instructions: The same student, the idea clicking, pleased and a little excited.
scenes.text: It hits us at a low angle, so the same light spreads out thinner.
Exactly. We're actually closest to the sun in January. You worked that out — I only asked.
